author_credibility.justification: All authors are affiliated with credible institutions having relevant expertise. The study involves 3 institutions and includes up to 2 authors with verifiable expertise.

research_question_and_methods.justification: The objectives are clear, focusing on the impact of mutations in the NTD of the spike protein on antibody recognition and pathogenicity, aligned with detailed methodologies that allow for reproducibility.
research_question_and_methods.quote: The present study describes two phenotypically distinct variants of SARS-CoV-2, differing by a mutation in the region of the genome encoding the NTD of the spike protein, and examines their recognition by neutralizing anti-spike antibodies as well as their pathogenesis in the Syrian hamster model.

results_and_conclusion.justification: Results lack sufficient clarity and may misrepresent findings, with reported phenomena not consistently supported by strong data interpretation.
results_and_conclusion.quote: Contrary to expectations, the Delta l.p. variant (without the insertion) caused more pronounced weight loss in the Syrian hamster model.
